forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: North Devon auditors clear accounts with no sustainability concerns
news_drafts.lead: North Devon Council's external auditors have found no significant weaknesses in its financial arrangements and anticipate issuing a clean audit opinion on the 2025/26 accounts. Bishop Fleming, the council's auditors, said the council has sound governance and sustainability arrangements in place. The council has meanwhile established a Councillor Budget Working Group to address a gap identified in its medium-term financial strategy — the plan showing expected spending and income over the next three to five years — but auditors did not flag this as a significant concern about the council's ability to balance its books. The council is also entering social housing provision as a Local Authority Registered Provider for the first time in over 20 years, a move that creates new statutory obligations; the council has engaged external consultants to ensure the governance arrangements are in place from the start.

findings.headline: The paper confirms no 'debt for yield' projects are in the current capital programme, following PWLB's withdrawal of loans for them.
findings.detail: The paper says the PWLB will no longer lend for debt-for-yield projects and that this would also mean no PWLB loans for the rest of the capital programme in that year. The Chief Finance Officer confirms there are no such projects in the current programme.
findings.matters: Councils with investment property plans need to know that PWLB lending for debt-for-yield schemes has been withdrawn, which affects how those schemes are funded.
findings.quote: The PWLB will no longer provide loans for

findings.headline: The revised Capital Financing Requirement at 31 March 2027 is £43,078k, against an original estimate of £43,219k.
findings.detail: The paper says the revised CFR is in line with the forecast, with a reduction of £141,000 estimated. The opening CFR at 1 April 2026 is £36,325k against £38,910k in the February forecast, which the paper attributes to 2025/26 capital programme slippage.
findings.matters: The gap between the opening CFR and the February forecast shows how carried-forward slippage flows into the underlying borrowing need.
findings.figures: £43,078k revised CFR at 31 March 2027; £43,219k original CFR; £36,325k opening CFR at 1 April 2026; £38,910k original opening CFR
findings.quote: with a slight reduction of £141,000 estimated.

findings.headline: No debt rescheduling has been undertaken in 2026/27 to date, although the paper says repayment and rescheduling opportunities have increased.
findings.detail: The paper says debt repayment or rescheduling will be considered only if it gives rise to long-term savings.
findings.matters: A council that has not rescheduled while the paper reports more opportunities is relevant to other councils considering the same options.
findings.quote: However, no debt rescheduling has been undertaken to date in the current financial year.

findings.headline: MUFG Corporate Markets forecasts rates to fall back over the next one to three years as inflation dampens.
findings.detail: The paper also sets out an upside risk of one 0.25% Bank Rate increase in November or December 2026 if second-round inflation effects become embedded. The council says falling rates mean its borrowing strategy is likely to remain short term.
findings.matters: The rate outlook determines whether a council locks in long-term funding now or keeps borrowing short, and other councils face the same decision.
findings.figures: CPI expected to hit 4.3% in early 2027 before falling towards 2% by 2028; one 0.25% Bank Rate increase as the upside risk
findings.quote: MUFG Corporate Markets forecasts rates to fall back over the next one to three years as inflation dampens

findings.headline: The 25-year PWLB certainty rate reached a high of 6.70% on 15/09/2026, against 6.20% on 01/04/2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the whole gilt and PWLB curve shifted higher over the half-year, with the bulk of low points in early April and the highs in mid-September. Spreads over gilts ranged from 0.59% at 50 years to 0.81% at 5 years.
findings.matters: The size of the swing across the half-year sets the price a council faces if it needs to replace maturing funding from the PWLB.
findings.quote: the general trend has been for the whole curve to shift higher on the back of inflation concerns
